sheet-1-1.description: The map part of Sheet 1 of the May 1925 Sanborn atlas of Hightstown, drawn at 100 feet to an inch in the lower right of the sheet and in a strip along its foot, below and to the right of the heavy line that encloses the title, the key map of the whole borough, the street index and the legend. North points to the right of the sheet. It covers the west end of the town along Stockton, which runs up the sheet from Summit to a five-way junction with Township Road, Stults Avenue and Eastwood, and then continues to the north-east. The strip at the foot follows Summit from Walter Street past Morrison Avenue, 1st Avenue and 2nd Avenue to Stockton. The area is thinly built: scattered frame dwellings with outbuildings on long narrow lots, many lots laid out but still empty, and a street marked not opened. Two public buildings stand out: Hightstown High School No. 1, a reinforced concrete building between Stults Avenue and Summit, and Hightstown High School No. 2, a fireproof building with a heating plant east of Stockton. Great Avenue on the right carries the long greenhouses of Braun Bros., with their boiler house. Water pipes are drawn along Stockton, Summit and Eastwood, with fire hydrants marked at several corners. The sheet's key map, index and title block are cut out of the mask and are not part of this map.
notes: Drawn at 100 ft to an inch; the key map on the same sheet is at 500 ft to an inch.

Walter St. is today's Dey Street; Township Rd. corresponds to Dutch Neck Road, Stults Av. to Harron Avenue and Eastwood to Oak Lane (from position; the five-way junction was not used as control because its modern position does not fit the drawn spacing).
Hightstown High School No. 1 and No. 2 and the Braun Bros. greenhouses are drawn.

Title, key map (500 ft to an inch, sheets 1 to 10), index and legend in the upper and left areas, cut out of the mask; map part 1 below and right of the heavy line at 100 ft to an inch: west end along Stockton, Township Rd., Stults Av., Eastwood, 2nd Av., Morrison Av., 1st Av., Summit and Walter St., with Hightstown High Schools No. 1 and No. 2 and Braun Bros. greenhouses. North points right. Only five of the ten sheets of the key are in this record (sheets 1 to 5).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 of the May 1925 Sanborn atlas of Hightstown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north at the top. It shows the business centre of the borough along Main Street, lettered N. Main north of Stockton and S. Main to the south, from the bridge at the top of the sheet down to Ward at the foot. Stockton enters from the upper left beside Railroad Avenue, and Morrison and Mercer Street come in from the left to meet S. Main in an open space near the middle of the sheet. The blocks along Main are closely built with brick and frame stores, offices and halls: the fire department engine house on Stockton, the Hightstown Title and Trust bank, the 1st National Bank, Scheible's hotel, a tinsmith and hardware warehouse, a bake shop, a chapel, the 1st Baptist Church and the Universalist Church. A cemetery lies behind the east side of S. Main. South of the cemetery the sheet is residential, with frame dwellings on long lots running east from S. Main towards the shore of Peddie Lake, which fills the right side of the sheet. The A. L. Duryea marble and granite works stand at the left edge near Morrison. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn in Main, Stockton, Mercer and Ward.
notes: Few junctions are drawn in full; Main / Mercer / Morrison is an open space and was hand-picked at the OpenStreetMap node.
Morrison no longer reaches Main today (modern Morrison Avenue ends at Railroad Avenue and Outcalt Street).
Ward at the foot is today's West Ward Street.
Downtown: N. and S. Main from Stockton to Ward, Railroad Av., Morrison, Mercer St., Peddie Lake on the east. 50 ft to an inch, north up. Few street junctions; Main / Mercer hand-picked.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 of the May 1925 Sanborn atlas of Hightstown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north at the top. It shows the grounds of the Peddie School, a college preparatory school for young men, which occupy nearly the whole sheet south of Ward and east of S. Main. Only the edges of these two streets are drawn: Ward along the top and S. Main along the left side, where a row of frame dwellings faces the street. The main school building, a large cross-shaped brick block with wings, stands in the upper middle of the campus, with a gymnasium and other brick buildings beside it, a power house to the east and several smaller buildings scattered across the grounds. Memorial Hall, a large E-shaped building, stands at the foot of the sheet. Peddie Lake runs down the right side of the sheet, its shore drawn as a curving line, with the open ground of the campus between the buildings and the water. Water pipes with hydrants are drawn along Ward and S. Main and into the grounds. The sheet has very little street network, so it was placed from a block corner at S. Main and Ward that is also drawn on sheet 2.
notes: Peddie School, college preparatory for young men, with Memorial Hall and a power house.
Placed from one block corner carried from sheet 2 with sheet 2's scale and rotation; low confidence.

Peddie School campus south of Ward, east of S. Main, Peddie Lake on the east. 50 ft to an inch, north up. No street junction drawn in full: anchored on a block corner carried from sheet 2 with sheet 2's scale and rotation.

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of Sheet 4 of the May 1925 Sanborn atlas of Hightstown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. It covers the south-west of the borough between Railroad Avenue and Liberty at the top, S. Academy and Ward on the right and S. Main at the foot. Mercer crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left to Ward, with Shingles Lane between Mercer and the railroad; South runs down the left side to S. Main, and Taylor Avenue leaves it towards the lower left. Most blocks hold frame dwellings with outbuildings on deep lots, with a public school on Mercer. The industrial area lies at the junction of Mercer, S. Academy and Ward: the Hightstown Manufacturing Company weaving, cutting and carding mill, the Hightstown Garage with its repair shops, and the Chamberlin and Field lumber yard with lumber sheds, a sash and blind storage and an office. A coal dealer's yard lies beside the railroad at the top. The large block between South, Mercer, Ward and S. Main is largely open in its centre. An inset in the left part of the sheet, outlined by a heavy line, belongs to another place on Mercer Street and is a separate part.
notes: Ward on the right is today's West Ward Street; South is South Street.
Placed from three points (two detected, one taken from a trial run); low confidence.
Hightstown Mfg. Co. weaving mill, Hightstown Garage and Chamberlin & Field lumber yard.

Mercer, S. Academy, Liberty, Railroad Av., Shingles Lane, South, Taylor Av., Ward and S. Main; Hightstown Mfg. Co., Hightstown Garage, Chamberlin & Field lumber yard. 50 ft to an inch, north to the upper right. Two parts: part 1 the main map; part 2 an inset outlined by a heavy line on the left (Mercer St. west of town with Pershing Av., a cemetery and A. L. Duryea granite works), not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Mercer Street west of town with Pershing Av., cemetery and A. L. Duryea granite works (no street junction that matches today's streets could be identified within the time spent; needs points carried from sheet-2 (Duryea works and the Mercer / Morrison junction are drawn on both) or parcel corners (step 6b)).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 of the May 1925 Sanborn atlas of Hightstown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. It covers the centre west of Main Street, from Outcalt at the top to S. Main at the foot and from S. Academy and Ward on the left to Stockton on the right. The Pennsylvania Railroad line crosses the sheet diagonally beside Railroad Avenue and Liberty, with sidings to a coal and lumber yard, a freight house and a long platform. Rogers Avenue, lettered also Morrison, runs down the middle of the sheet to Mercer, and Church, Forman and Wood are short cross streets. North of the railroad the blocks are lined with frame dwellings, many of them in rows, and the Jamesburg Shirt Company factory stands near S. Academy. South of the railroad the sheet is more mixed: the 1st Methodist Episcopal Church on Stockton, an opera house used for motion pictures, the Central Hotel, a furniture and undertaking store, the post office near S. Main and stores along Mercer and S. Main. A large open area at the lower right lies between the railroad and Main Street.
notes: The Pennsylvania Railroad line through the sheet is abandoned today.
Rogers Av. is lettered with Morrison in brackets; Ward is today's West Ward Street.
Drawn scale fits about 6.9 px/ft against about 7.3 to 7.4 on sheets 2 and 4: the sheet may be drawn slightly small or one of its four points is off.

Centre west of Main: Outcalt, S. Academy, Railroad Av. with the Pennsylvania R.R. (abandoned today), Wood, Rogers Av. (Morrison), Church, Stockton, Forman, Liberty, Mercer, Morrison, Ward, S. Main. 50 ft to an inch, north to the upper right.
